requirement:
Only current results whose captured source inputs match the current source
and whose build configurations are compatible contribute counts to saved
execution-coverage checks under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`. Results with changed
inputs are identified as stale; results of unknown compatibility are
identified as unavailable. Both are excluded from combined totals.

A filtered run preserves the provenance of unselected results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`. It does not make those
results fresh when their recorded inputs no longer match. Their process
reports and matching captured source remain available until replacement or
removal of the build artifacts.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately cover each obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`.

**Source and input changes make a result stale.**
- `src/execution_coverage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[source_and_build_inputs_invalidate_on_addition_removal_and_dirty_content]` checks that `fresh` is false after each of these changes:
  - a modified source file;
  - an added source file;
  - a removed source file;
  - changes to `Cargo.lock`, `Cargo.toml` and member manifests;
  - removal of `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`;
  - a new `rust-toolchain.toml`;
  - new or changed files under watched directories, including one under `node_modules`;
  - a watched path that did not exist when the run was captured.
- The same test asserts that `fresh` returns to true after each change is reverted.
- `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[real_build_captures_dependency_files_and_environment_for_read_only_freshness_checks]` does this end to end with a real build.
  - It asserts the capture includes `include_str!` data, `rerun-if-changed` files, `build.rs` and `Cargo.lock`.
  - It asserts that changing the included file or the build-input file makes `coverage-check` report "stale coverage".
  - It asserts that changing the compiler or build environment value does the same.
  - It asserts that reverting each change clears the stale report, and that the retained files are unchanged by checking.

**Build configuration compatibility.**
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cargo_launch_metadata_does_not_invalidate_but_caller_build_environment_does]` shows that Cargo launch metadata does not make a result stale. It also shows that changes to `CC`, `RUSTFLAGS`, `CARGO_PROFILE_*`, a target linker variable and a build-input variable do.
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source]` records a `build-b` result after `build-a` results. It then asserts that only one record is selected and that its configuration is `build-b`. Results from an incompatible configuration therefore do not contribute.

**Stale and unavailable results are excluded from totals.**
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[stale_or_unknown_records_publish_no_current_file_totals]` first checks a fresh result and sees `code.rs: 2/2 (100.0%)`.
  - After a source change, the check reports "stale coverage", fails, and prints no per-file totals or percentages.
  - After the run's schema is set to 99, the compatibility is unknown. The check fails with "cannot establish the current test set" and still prints no totals.
  - The test also asserts that the SQLite store and the profile file remain.
- `unreadable_history_cannot_reintroduce_an_older_success` covers four failure modes: invalid metadata, missing source, unsupported schema and missing profile. In each, the check fails and no positive counts come from an older success.
- `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[focused_recollection_leaves_only_the_unselected_result_stale_with_its_original_sources]` mixes a fresh result with a stale one. The check fails, and no totals or percentages are shown.

**A filtered run preserves provenance without making the unselected result fresh.**
- `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[focused_recollection_leaves_only_the_unselected_result_stale_with_its_original_sources]` re-collects only one test after a source change.
  - The unselected result stays `!fresh`, and the rerun result is fresh.
  - The unselected result keeps its original attempt id, run id and captured source (`"fn a() {}"`).
  - The rerun result carries the new source.
  - The check reports "stale coverage" for only the unselected test.
- Retention of the process reports is supported by the profile-file existence assertion in `stale_or_unknown_records_publish_no_current_file_totals`. It is also covered by `saved_reports_preserve_profiles_sources_and_child_union`, which asserts that profile contents and sources are retained and that the archived record is not fresh. That test is not marked for freshness, but it is directly relevant.

No uncovered obligation or weak assertion was found. I read `load_saved` and `check_saved` only to confirm that freshness depends on the run's configuration matching the active configuration and on the input check. That is consistent with the tests above.

text: :::{req} index.freshness
Only current results whose captured source inputs match the current source
and whose build configurations are compatible contribute counts to saved
execution-coverage checks under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`. Results with changed
inputs are identified as stale; results of unknown compatibility are
identified as unavailable. Both are excluded from combined totals.
A filtered run preserves the provenance of unselected results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`. It does not make those
results fresh when their recorded inputs no longer match. Their process
reports and matching captured source remain available until replacement or
removal of the build artifacts.
:::{req} index.selection
Saved execution-coverage checks read the current coverage set under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.current` from SQLite. Each check
uses one coherent database snapshot of test identities, states, provenance,
and processed measurements, so a replacement or update cannot mix results
from different snapshots within the same check.
Checks do not search historical runs or use a separate report-selection
metadata cache. Current test identities, states, and provenance can be read
without loading their detailed measurements.
Only current results with complete, available measurements contribute to
coverage under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`.
Pending, running, and unavailable entries are reported under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`. Checking does not build
or execute tests and never restores a superseded attempt.
:::{req} storage.replace
After preparation and selection discovery succeed, and before any selected
test starts, Habeas atomically establishes the new coverage set:
- An unfiltered workspace invocation clears the entire previous set,
including results for tests that no longer exist. This includes
`habeas coverage` with no supplied arguments and `habeas test`.
- An invocation with an explicit package or binary restriction, test filter,
partition, or ignored-only selection is filtered. It clears results for all
selected test identities and preserves unselected results within the
active build configuration.
- Every selected test receives a pending entry without measurements.
Native default filters and the default handling of ignored tests still apply
to an unfiltered workspace invocation. `--run-ignored all` alone does not make
a workspace invocation filtered.
A selected test that never starts because of fail-fast, interruption, or
execution startup failure remains unavailable. Its previous result does not
become available again. A filtered selection containing no tests leaves the
current results and active configuration unchanged; an empty unfiltered
workspace selection clears the previous set.
If the atomic replacement cannot be committed, the command reports the
failure and starts no tests. The previously committed coverage set and active
configuration remain unchanged.
